stories.title: Delhi man stabs 9 cops at police station; held after shoot-out
stories.summary: Police said the accused had a previous case registered against him at Daryaganj in 2022 under Section 324 of the IPC for causing hurt with a dangerous weapon.
stories.text:
Jignasa Sinha is a Special Correspondent at Hindustan Times in New Delhi. With more than six years of reporting experience, she covers crime and policing in the national capital. Her beats also include Delhi prisons, the Delhi Fire Services and Delhi courts, while she regularly reports on gender, labour and social justice. Over the course of her career, Jignasa has reported on major criminal investigations, international crime syndicates, high-profile cyber fraud cases, law-and-order developments, protests, disasters and public institutions. Her reporting combines breaking news with in-depth, long form, human interest stories that examine the human impact of public policy, policing and the criminal justice system. In addition to reporting for the newspaper, she contributes to the Hindustan Times website and app, and plays an active role in coordinating on-ground coverage of major developments and breaking news across Delhi. Before joining Hindustan Times, Jignasa worked at The Indian Express newspaper in New Delhi, where she spent five years covering crime, Delhi airport, courts and health. She began her journalism career as an intern at an AI magazine in Bengaluru while pursuing her postgraduate diploma in multimedia journalism at the Indian Institute of Journalism and New Media.

# Delhi man stabs 9 cops at police station; held after shoot-out

## Police said the accused had a previous case registered against him at Daryaganj in 2022 under Section 324 of the IPC for causing hurt with a dangerous weapon.

A 30-year-old man allegedly went on a stabbing spree with a pocket knife on Monday afternoon, injuring at least nine police officers – five at the Jama Masjid police station and four at another location nearby during an encounter where he was shot six times – officials and eyewitnesses said.

The alleged stabber, identified as Md Nabeel, sustained six gunshot wounds, all in his legs, during an encounter in the Bazar Chitli Qabar area near Daryaganj, where he fled on a stolen scooter. He is undergoing treatment at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, where he suffered heavy blood loss, officials said.

According to police, the dramatic chain of events unfolded when Nabeel allegedly entered the Jama Masjid police station following complaints by his mother and sister, who were there around 1:30-2pm to file a complaint against him. Nabeel lived with his family in the Kala Mahal area of Jama Masjid and was unemployed.

Police said Nabeel attacked the policemen and fled from the station, all within three minutes.

Rohit Rajbir Singh, deputy commissioner of police (Central), said Nabeel “appeared to be mentally stable, but was very aggressive.”

“The mother told police officers that she was disturbed because he constantly harassed her and her daughter for money. He would hit them as well. They went to Sub-Inspector Ajay to complain, and he first called Nabeel to counsel him. At first, Nabeel told SI Ajay over the phone that he couldn’t come. When Ajay insisted that a complaint was being filed and his family members were there, he got angry and said he was coming.”

## Attack at the Police Station

Around 2:30pm, police said Nabeel entered the Jama Masjid police station. Two police officials, both of whom asked not to be identified, said Nabeel was “aggressive” and shouted in the reception area.

“He was demanding the person’s name who had called him there. SI Ajay came forward. Nabeel charged at him and tried to attack him with a knife. Four to five staff rushed to save Ajay and detain Nabeel. They jumped at Nabeel, but he attacked them all. Some staff got very scared and rushed inside the police station. They picked up batons and called for backup, but Nabeel ran outside. Others lay injured and screamed for help as Nabeel ran outside,” one of the officials cited above said.

The second official said that the incident happened at the reception area where only a few staffers were present. Nabeel’s mother and sister witnessed the entire episode.

DCP Singh said two personnel ran behind him, but he was quick. “In front of the station, he stopped a person and threatened him with his knife. He snatched his bike and fled. The incident left five persons injured, including two sub-inspectors, two head constables, and one ASI. SI Ajay, SI Arvind, and HC Harender suffered severe injuries to their necks and faces. ASI Shri Krishna and HC Baljeet also suffered injuries,” the DCP added.

## Encounter and Police Investigation

After the incident, multiple teams from four police stations, the special staff, and the Anti-Auto Theft Squad were formed to trace Nabeel. “The teams searched nearby areas and traced him within two hours. By 4:30pm, the team had traced the vehicle and found Nabeel. As the team warned him and asked him to surrender, he again turned aggressive and started attacking policemen around him. Despite the threat, the policemen exhibited restraint and fired below the waist. During the controlled firing, eight rounds were fired. Six rounds hit Nabeel in the legs,” DCP Singh said.

The four injured during the encounter were identified as constables Ankit, Jayant, Lokesh, and Parminder, and were shifted to LNJP Hospital.

“The accused has one previous criminal involvement in a case registered under Section 324 IPC (causing hurt by dangerous weapon) at Daryaganj in 2022. We are lodging three cases against him – one for attacking policemen at the station, one for stealing a bike, and a third for again attacking policemen at Chitli Qabar area,” said DCP Singh.

Police said Nabeel was married, but his wife left him due to his anger issues. “He has two brothers who work different jobs. All of them complained about his behaviour,” another official said.

stories.title: Non-bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in 2018 defamation case
stories.text:
A Delhi court on Monday issued a non-bailable warrant against YouTuber Dhruv Rathee in a 2018 defamation case filed by Vikas Pandey over allegations made in a video that the BJP’s Information and Technology cell had attempted to bribe him.

Judicial Magistrate First Class Anam Rais Khan of Saket courts issued the warrant and listed the matter for December 3. The case relates to a video Rathee created in May 2018 alleging that the BJP IT cell had attempted to bribe Pandey. Rathee tweeted the video, which was later retweeted by Arvind Kejriwal, who was then Delhi chief minister.

Pandey subsequently initiated defamation proceedings, alleging that the circulation of the video had harmed his reputation. In his complaint, he alleged that Rathee, who ordinarily resides in Germany, had published and circulated a video titled “BJP IT Cell Part II” containing false allegations against him.

Rathee was first summoned in the case in July 2019. In October, the court issued fresh summons to him at the Gurugram address he had submitted after being informed that he was at his residence there. The court had earlier directed that the fresh summons be issued at the Gurugram address.

Later in October, Judicial Magistrate First Class Rahul Jain, who is hearing the defamation case, issued bailable warrants against Rathee after the court was informed that his premises in Gurugram were locked. The bailable warrants followed the fresh summons issued to him.

Pandey had earlier sought preponement of the matter, saying Rathee, who ordinarily resides abroad, was in India at the time in connection with the CJP protests.

The latest non-bailable warrant was issued as the court continued proceedings in the defamation case, with the matter now listed for December 3.

stories.title: SC to hear on November 25 pleas of Sharjeel Imam, Umar Khalid seeking bail in UAPA case
stories.summary: In their pleas before the Supreme Court, the activists have sought bail, contending that the prosecution has failed to examine protected witnesses and the one-year embargo imposed by the Supreme Court is nearing its expiry
stories.text:
The Supreme Court is slated to hear on Wednesday pleas of activists Sharjeel Imam and Umar Khalid challenging a Delhi High Court order denying them bail in an Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) case related to the alleged "larger conspiracy" behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.

As per the cause list, a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana is likely to hear the matter.

In their pleas before the Supreme Court, the activists have sought bail, contending that the prosecution has failed to examine protected witnesses and the one-year embargo imposed by the Supreme Court is nearing its expiry.

**
Also read | The continued custody in Delhi Riots cases is an injustice**

The petition by Mr. Imam contended that the chargesheet was filed on September 25, 2020, in which 18 accused face trial and the prosecution has cited more than 900 witnesses, including 47 protected witnesses.

Mr. Khalid, in his plea, also cited the failure to examine protected witnesses and said the expiry of the one-year embargo would mean that his continued incarceration would violate Article 21 of the Constitution.

Mr. Imam submitted that despite spending six years and nine months as undertrial, the prosecution has failed to examine even a single witness.

The Delhi High Court on September 30 refused to grant bail to Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam in a case under UAPA on the "larger conspiracy" behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.

Observing that it was bound by "judicial discipline", the high court said it could not modify the Supreme Court's January 5 order, which had asked the two accused to seek bail either after the examination of protected witnesses or the expiry of one year, whichever was earlier.

Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam challenged the trial court's July 4 decision rejecting their bail pleas for the third time since their arrest.

The trial court had rejected the bail applications, saying it had "no option but to follow" the Supreme Court's January 5 order and, therefore, could neither entertain the plea nor grant any relief.

The High Court had noted that while denying bail to the two accused in January, the top court had said their roles were distinct from the other co-accused, and they were the "ideological drivers" of the alleged conspiracy.

Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam have been booked under UAPA on allegations of being among the masterminds of the February 2020 riots that left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.

The violence erupted during protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA), 2019, and the National Register of Citizens (NRC).

Activist Khalid Saifi and former AAP councillor Tahir Hussain, among others, were also booked for their alleged involvement in the larger conspiracy case, being investigated by Delhi Police's Special Cell.

Mr. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.

On September 2, 2025, a high court division bench denied bail to Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam.

On January 5, the Supreme Court upheld the verdict but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.

A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and N.V. Anjaria had then observed that there was a prima facie case against Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam under the UAPA.

The Supreme Court, while rejecting their contention of delay in trial, had said Mr. Khalid and Mr. Imam, who have been in jail since 2020, could file fresh bail applications after the examination of protected witnesses or after one year from the date of the order.

On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six-month interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad and referred the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA, in view of the stringent prerequisites for bail, to a larger bench.

stories.title: Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on December 16
stories.summary: Hasina urges Dhaka to arrange her return on the national airline, as government says she can only be extradited.
stories.text:
Sheikh Hasina, the former prime minister of Bangladesh who was overthrown more than two years ago, plans to return home from exile in India on December 16, her spokesperson said, as the government said she can only return through extradition.

Hasina went into exile in August 2024 after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule.

list of 4 items- list 1 of 4Spontaneous or orchestrated? Violent pro-Hasina protests rock Bangladesh
- list 2 of 4Bangladesh prosecutor warns Hasina faces execution if she returns
- list 3 of 4Sheikh Hasina must return to Bangladesh to face her sentence
- list 4 of 4Will Sheikh Hasina return to Bangladesh?

She was later sentenced to death by a Bangladesh court in her absence for ordering the deadly crackdown on the uprising in which hundreds of protesters were killed.

Hasina rejected the verdict and has said she is ready to fight the case once she is back.

Announcing her plan to return on the anniversary of the end of her country’s 1971 liberation war with Pakistan, she urged Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her flight on the national airline.

“Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” spokesperson Syed Mozammel Ali said in a statement on Tuesday.

## Government position ‘very clear’

Abu Abdullah M Saleh, Prime Minister Rahman’s press secretary, told the Associated Press news agency that the government would stick to its position on Hasina’s extradition as a convict.

“My government’s stand is very clear. She has been convicted in a tribunal. We have sought her extradition,” he said by phone.

Hasina is expected to be arrested upon her return and sent to jail.

Aminul Islam, chief prosecutor of Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal, which sentenced Hasina to death, said it was unreasonable for a convicted fugitive to expect the government to arrange her return.

The judiciary had earlier said that Hasina would not be able to appeal her death sentence as she missed the required deadline and there would be no legal basis to stop her execution.

In Bangladesh, presidential clemency is allowed, but Hasina has never sought that in earlier statements and has rejected the verdict outright.

The United Nations has said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest that forced Hasina from power.

Hasina’s father led the war against Pakistan and after independence was the first leader of the new People’s Republic of Bangladesh.

He was killed in a military coup in 1975, along with most of his family members. Hasina and her younger sister survived as they were out of the country.

stories.title: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship docked at a naval base in Libya
stories.summary: Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, claiming that sea drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault.
stories.text:
KYIV, Ukraine — Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday, claiming that maritime drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day.

Ukrainian forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Zelenskyy. The ship, the Merkury, was one of Russia's newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbor, he said in a post on X.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to comment on the attack, saying that Russia's Defense Ministry would provide more information "if deemed to be appropriate."

The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometers (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces.

Ukraine has at times embarrassed Moscow during the war with attacks such as Operation Spiderweb in June 2025, when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft parked at air bases across Russia. Along the roughly 1,250-kilometer (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine, Kyiv's drones and ground robots are helping hold back Russia's bigger army.

At the same time, Russia's missiles and drones have devastated Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter and damaged civilian buildings.

A Russian strike on a five-story apartment block in a village near Kyiv killed 11 people, regional police said Monday. A 7-year-old child and a 79-year-old woman were pulled alive from the rubble after the Sunday morning attack, rescue services said.

Three people were killed Monday in a Russian strike on a hospital in the city of Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine, the regional military administration said. Two other people were killed when Russian forces struck a vehicle that bore markings indicating it was evacuating residents from the eastern city of Kramatorsk, authorities said.

Also on Monday, the European Commission proposed a new round of sanctions to keep economic pressure on Moscow, targeting dozens of Russian banks, cracking down on crypto platforms and slapping bans on sports teams and athletes competing under the country's flag.

The proposals, put forward by Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, must be endorsed by all 27 European Union member countries before they can enter into force. The process can take weeks, and the planned measures are likely to be modified.

The bloc has already hit more than 4,700 people and entities, including President Vladimir Putin, and several energy companies.

### Zelenskyy lauds Ukrainian attacks from Siberia to Libya

Zelenskyy described Sunday's attack as "exemplary" and said "the targets we set were achieved."

"We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons," he said.

Ukraine has hit Russian oil refineries as far away as western Siberia and Russian warships in the Mediterranean, Zelenskyy noted in a video address to a meeting of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

An oil refinery in Russia's western Rostov region halted work Monday after what Gov. Yuri Slyusar said was a "massive" Ukrainian drone and missile attack that lasted more than six hours. Ukraine's General Staff said the refinery, located just a few dozen kilometers (miles) from the Ukrainian border, can process up to 55 million barrels of oil a year and was on fire after the attack.

Russian officials also reported Monday a Ukrainian attack on industrial sites in Russia's Perm region, more than 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) from Ukraine. One person was killed in the attack, and 56 Ukrainian drones were downed, Perm Gov. Dmitri Makhonin said.

"We keep finding ways to get back on our feet after every Russian attack," Zelenskyy said.

Ukrainian forces also struck the Russian dry cargo ship MV Angara, which Zelenskyy said Moscow used to transport weapons. He added that the forces also destroyed a Ka-27 military helicopter that was on the Merkury.

Ukrainian forces are operating in western Libya under a covert deal endorsed by the West, using the North African country's territory to strike a Russian tanker in the Mediterranean in March, according to Libyan officials.

The Ukrainian forces, most of them drone experts, were operating mainly at an air base in the coastal city of Misrata, but also in other military facilities in the capital of Tripoli and the coastal town of Zawiya, the officials told The Associated Press earlier this year. They spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential matters.

Sunday's attack severely damaged the Russian corvette at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya, according to two Libyan officials, although Zelenskyy claimed it was sunk.

Benghazi residents heard loud explosions and saw flames at the base early Sunday. Civil defense units rushed to the site and extinguished the fire, authorities in eastern Libya said.

The vessel had docked to refuel and take on supplies as part of an agreement between Russia and the eastern-based government in Libya, a statement said without providing details about the vessel or its cargo.

The government in eastern Libya sent a letter to U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres and the U.N. Security Council, calling for an international investigation into the potential use of western Libya to prepare and launch the attack.

### Libyan officials say 2 sea drones hit Russian warship

Libyan officials who were briefed on the attack told AP that at least four drones were intercepted while two hit the corvette, which is designed to patrol coastal waters and escort other ships.

At least 10 people, including Libyan and Russian nationals, were wounded in the attack, one of the officials said.

The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.

Ambrey, a U.K.-based maritime security and risk intelligence firm, said that some of the explosions at the Benghazi Naval Base were likely caused by the detonation of ammunition aboard the Merkury.

Hours after the warship attack, another sea drone strike hit a Maltese-flagged commercial vessel sailing off Benghazi, the Libyan coast guard said.

### The Russian cargo ship was sanctioned, Ukraine says

Ukraine's Security Service, or SBU, said the cargo ship MV Angara was sanctioned and used to transport Russian military equipment, while the Merkury regularly escorted Russian naval convoys, including guarding the MV Angara.

The drones were delivered to a designated location and launched from a "mother ship" near the target, the SBU said.

Russian defenses tried to intercept the attacking drones, it said.

"Ukraine's defense forces have once again shown that the Russian navy and its logistics have no safe routes," the SBU said.

stories.title: China sentences official to death for spying for foreign country
stories.summary: Accused official leaked national secrets to unnamed country and received payments worth over $150,000, state-linked publisher saysA Chinese official has been sentenced to death for spying for a foreign country, a government-linked publisher has said.Gold Wall Press, a publishing company associated with China’s…
stories.text:
A Chinese official has been sentenced to death for spying for a foreign country, a government-linked publisher has said.

Gold Wall Press, a publishing company associated with China’s national administration of state secrets protection, said the convicted person was surnamed Ma and was approached and recruited by an unnamed foreign intelligence service while working abroad.

Chinese courts typically do not publish information about state security cases, but in recent years the powerful ministry of state security and Gold Wall Press have increasingly publicised arrests, as well as using social media, movies and comics to promote warnings about espionage.

The statement on Monday said Ma had signed a cooperation agreement containing clauses on “confidentiality” and “loyalty” and received fixed monthly payments. In total, it said, he provided 35 pieces of information that were classified as national secrets and received payments worth more than 1m yuan ($150,000).

An intelligence operative identified as Kailin “frequently arranged to meet with Ma, hoping to engage with him more”, citing an interest in learning Chinese, the statement said. Kailin later introduced him to a colleague who threatened to report his earlier disclosures to Chinese authorities if he refused to cooperate.

After returning to China, Ma continued to gather intelligence for the foreign agency, which provided him with a laptop, the statement said. He used his position to collect material from classified documents during the day and transmitted it overseas at night via an espionage website.

The statement did not identify the countries involved, or say when or where he was sentenced or whether he had already been executed.

The case comes as US intelligence has been publicising its own efforts to recruit sources in China. The five most-viewed videos on the CIA’s YouTube channel are recruiting advertisements in Mandarin.

“This shocking case serves as yet another wake-up call,” the Gold Wall Press said, warning that foreign intelligence agencies were “cunning” and used emotional ties, financial interests and threats to recruit people in key positions.

The statement also urged officials to remain vigilant, strengthen their loyalty to the Communist party, protect state secrets and guard against foreign recruitment.

In 2023 Beijing broadened its anti-espionage law, expanding the definition of espionage and strengthening the investigative powers of state security authorities. The following year it revised its state secrets law to extend restrictions on sensitive information to so-called “work secrets”.

stories.title: Appeals court renews Trump bid for federal jurisdiction in hush-money case
stories.summary: The ruling could clear the way for Trump to argue prosecutors relied on evidence protected by presidential immunity.
stories.text:
A federal appeals court has revived United States President Donald Trump’s bid to transfer his New York criminal hush-money case to federal court, months after a district judge rejected the effort for a third time.

On Monday, a three-judge panel of the 2nd Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a lower court ruling that had kept the case in New York state court.

In a two-page order, the 2nd Circuit panel said it disagreed with the late US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein’s denial of Trump’s request for the “removal” of his case to federal court.

The appeals court said Hellerstein had “erred in holding that removal is categorically unavailable in a state criminal case” after conviction.

It directed a federal judge in Manhattan to consider whether the proceedings could be brought under federal jurisdiction.

In a written statement provided to The Associated Press news agency, a spokesperson for Trump’s legal team said the president “appreciates the 2nd Circuit’s prompt and correct ruling, as he continues to win against Democrat weaponization of our Justice System”.

Trump has sought to use presidential immunity in federal court to have his conviction overturned. He was convicted on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records in 2024, though he has denied any wrongdoing.

## Trump’s New York criminal conviction

The case stems from a $130,000 “hush money” payment made shortly before the 2016 presidential election to adult film performer Stormy Daniels.

Daniels had claimed she had an affair with the Republican leader while he was married — an allegation he denies — and prosecutors alleged that the money was intended to buy her silence during a tense campaign season.

Trump ultimately won the 2016 presidential election, ushering him into his first term in public office.

The payment was made through Trump’s former lawyer and fixer Michael Cohen. Prosecutors argued that Trump fudged his business records to pass off his reimbursements to Cohen as legal expenses, thereby concealing them from voters.

While falsifying business records is normally a misdemeanour offence, it can be charged as a felony if done in service of another crime. In Trump’s case, prosecutors said he violated state election laws.

In May 2024, a New York jury found him guilty, making Trump the first US president to be convicted of a crime.

At a sentencing hearing in January 2025 — shortly before his second term as president began — Trump received an unconditional discharge, meaning he faced neither imprisonment nor a financial penalty. But his conviction remains on the record.

## Why does Trump want the case heard in federal court?

For years, Trump has sought to overturn that conviction.

Monday’s ruling leaves the jury’s guilty verdict intact, but it also clears the way for the president to seek a hearing in federal court.

He is expected to argue that state prosecutors secured his conviction by relying on evidence that would have been shielded by presidential immunity in federal court.

His legal team is likely to point to a landmark 2024 ruling as justification for that argument.

At the time, the Supreme Court’s conservative majority ruled that presidents could enjoy “presumptive immunity” for any “official acts” conducted while in office.

What constitutes an “official act”, however, is an open question. Previously, the Supreme Court had only conferred immunity to actions taken within a president’s constitutional authority.

Monday’s ruling reverses a series of setbacks for Trump’s legal team.

In August, federal judge Hellerstein rejected Trump’s third attempt to transfer the case, finding that the president’s arguments were insufficient to justify moving it out of state court.

Hellerstein, a senior federal judge in Manhattan’s Southern District of New York, died last month at the age of 92.

The move also stalls Trump’s state-level appeal in New York’s Appellate Division, which heard arguments earlier this month but has yet to rule on his challenge.

A federal judge has been directed to rule promptly on whether the case should indeed be transferred from New York state court to federal jurisdiction, although no deadline has been set.

stories.title: What happens if a nuclear weapon explodes in space?
stories.summary: Earth's atmosphere offers protection from a nuclear blast in space, but satellites are more exposed. We explain how radiation could damage them, why the effects can linger and what protection is possible.
stories.text:
A nuclear explosion in space would be unlikely to cause widespread injuries on Earth. But it could disable satellites that provide services we depend on every day, including some that save lives.

In the United States, satellite failures could make it harder for emergency crews to communicate in remote areas. If GPS were also disrupted, drivers and pilots could lose navigation guidance, and financial networks could lose a source of precise time.

We have some idea of what would happen because it's already been done.

## What does history teach us?

On the evening of July 8, 1962, people in Hawaii held "watch-the-bomb parties" and followed the countdown on shortwave radio. Then the night sky lit up. The United States had detonated a nuclear weapon about 400 kilometers (250 miles) above the Pacific. The test was called Starfish Prime.

An electromagnetic pulse knocked out some streetlights in Hawaii, and some Pacific radio links briefly went down. The glow faded within minutes, but some satellites failed months later.

## How does the physics change in space?

The air was too thin for a conventional fireball to form or for a destructive shock wave to reach the ground. Charged particles made denser air below glow, creating an artificial aurora. The atmosphere also absorbed much of the initial radiation.

Satellites are especially vulnerable because they orbit above most of the atmosphere that shields people on the ground from the initial radiation.

In orbit, the initial burst of X-rays can damage spacecraft right away. But Earth's magnetic field can also trap electrons released after the blast, as it did after Starfish Prime. Satellites receive another dose each time they cross the resulting radiation belt. Over time, that exposure can damage electronics and solar panels.

## Which systems would be exposed?

That would depend on where the explosion happened and which satellites crossed the radiation belt. GPS satellites send signals that help phones, planes and ships work out where they are. They orbit about 20,200 kilometers above Earth and could keep working even if satellites closer to Earth failed.

But satellites do different jobs. A ship's emergency beacon can use GPS to work out its location, then send it to rescuers through a separate satellite network. If part of that network failed, the alert could take longer to get through.

## Is it legal, and could it be detected?

The 1967 Outer Space Treaty bars its parties from placing nuclear weapons in orbit. The 1963 Limited Test Ban Treaty prohibits its parties from carrying out nuclear explosions in space.

The Outer Space Treaty has no dedicated system for checking what spacecraft carry. A detonation is easier to detect because US satellite sensors are designed to pick up the signals it gives off.

## Can the US protect itself?

Shielding could help protect satellite electronics, and backups could keep some services running. During a GPS outage, pilots over the contiguous US can use ground-based navigation aids. Operators could launch replacements, but those satellites could still face lingering radiation or debris.

Radiation could leave many satellites intact but unable to steer. If two objects collided, fragments from the crash could hit other satellites, creating more debris and triggering further collisions. If enough debris built up for the chain reaction to keep going on its own, it could continue even if no new satellites were launched. This is known as Kessler syndrome.

Whether an explosion would trigger such a cascade is uncertain. If it did, the debris could endanger replacement satellites for years.

## Could radioactive fallout reach the ground?

Some radioactive particles could enter the atmosphere and eventually settle on the ground. But a blast in space is too far away to sweep up the soil and water that carry fallout from a surface explosion.

As the particles disperse, their radioactivity decreases over time. The concentrated local fallout that can expose people near a ground-level blast to high doses would be unlikely.

stories.title: Stock market open today or not? BSE, NSE closed on 24 Nov for Guru Nanak Jayanti? Check holiday calendar
stories.summary: Indian equity markets will close on 24 November for Guru Nanak Jayanti. MCX will pause morning trading and reopen from 5 pm to 11:30 pm, while NCDEX remains closed all day. Christmas is the final scheduled market holiday of 2026.
stories.text:
The Indian stock market will remain closed on Tuesday, 24 November, on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev, also known as Guru Nanak Jayanti. While equity markets will remain shut, trading arrangements across commodity exchanges will differ. The Multi-Commodity Exchange of India (MCX MCX will suspend trading during its morning session, from 9 am to 5 pm, on Tuesday, 24 November. However, the exchange will reopen for the evening session, with trading scheduled from 5 pm to 11:30 pm, according to its website. NCDEX, on the other hand, will remain closed throughout the day. This means traders in commodity markets should check the exchange-wise schedule before placing orders, as the holiday will not affect all segments in the same way. Following the 24 November closure for Guru Nanak Jayanti, the next scheduled trading holiday for the BSE and NSE will be on 25 December, on account of Christmas. Of the 16 stock market holidays scheduled for 2026, 14 have already been observed. The exchanges were closed twice in April — on 3 April for Good Friday and 14 April for Dr B.R. Ambedkar Jayanti. Other holidays during the year included Maharashtra Day on 1 May, Bakri Id on 28 May, Muharram on 26 June and Ganesh Chaturthi on 14 September. Markets also remained shut on 2 October for Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti and 20 October for Dussehra. The most recent holiday before Tuesday was 10 November, for Diwali. With the 24 November holiday, only the Christmas closure remains on the 2026 trading calendar. The market holiday comes at a time when Indian equities are drawing renewed interest from foreign investors and moving closer to their previous record highs. The Nifty 50 is now around 2% below its all-time high of 26,373.20, while the Sensex is less than 3% away from its record peak of 86,159. A sharp turnaround in foreign institutional investor (FII) flows has been a major driver of the recent rally. Foreign investors, who had been among the biggest sellers in Indian equities, have extended their buying streak to 15 consecutive sessions. Their net purchases in domestic equities have crossed ₹1.3 lakh crore so far in November. Foreign investors have been reallocating funds away from global artificial intelligence-linked trades towards India's liquid and relatively reasonably valued large-cap stocks, particularly banking shares. Private lenders have helped push the banking index to successive record highs. A stronger rupee, softer crude oil prices and resilient second-quarter earnings have further supported the positive sentiment towards Indian equities. With the benchmark indices nearing record levels and foreign inflows gathering pace, investors will be watching whether the rally can regain momentum when trading resumes after the Guru Nanak Jayanti holiday. Nagaraj Shetti, Senior Technical Research Analyst at HDFC Securities, said the market witnessed sharp profit-booking on Monday after a strong rally over the past few weeks. The Nifty 50 slipped from highs near the 26,000 mark and ended the session nearly 450 points lower. He noted that the daily chart formed a long bearish candle after the index opened higher. The candle engulfed the previous session's long bullish candle, indicating a potential shift in market sentiment. According to Shetti, the pattern resembles a Bearish Dark Cloud Cover, which signals a possible short-term downside reversal. However, the pattern will be confirmed only if the market sees further weakness in the subsequent session. Monday's trading range stood at around 648 points. Shetti said the Nifty 50's short-term trend has turned bearish following its sharp upward move. However, he believes the ongoing correction could be short-lived, with the market likely to attempt a recovery from lower levels. He identified 25,000 as an immediate support level, while a decisive rebound could face strong resistance around 26,000. *Disclaimer: This story is for educational purposes only. stories.title: IIFCL IPO: Govt plans to sell part of its stake, company to issue fresh shares
stories.summary: The government aims to partially divest its shareholding in India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd through an initial public offering. The IPO is expected to occur by the end of the current fiscal year, according to an official statement. IIFCL will issue fresh shares to raise capital alongside the government stake…
stories.text:
The Cabinet had earlier this year approved the IPO and listing of India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd (IIFCL), and the work is on to file a draft paper with market regulator Sebi for approval.

Without disclosing the quantum of stake dilution, the official said that while the government will reduce its stake by an offer for sale, IFCL will issue fresh shares to raise capital in the IPO.

Set up in 2006, IIFCL is a wholly-owned government company providing long-term finances to viable infrastructure projects and is registered as a non-deposit taking non-banking finance company with the RBI.

As of March 31, 2026, IIFCL's gross sanctions stood at over Rs 3.64 lakh crore to about 890 projects under direct lending, takeout finance and refinance, credit enhancement, InVIT and bonds. Cumulative disbursements under these schemes stood at over Rs 1.89 lakh crore.

The proceeds from the government stake sale in IIFCL will add to the government's disinvestment kitty. In the current fiscal year, the disinvestment proceeds stand at Rs 55,757 crore so far.

This rally was largely propelled by foreign institutional investors, who contributed record-setting inflows exceeding Rs 1 lakh crore. Motivated by lower crude oil prices and…
stories.text:
The 30-share BSE benchmark Sensex jumped 7,976.46 points, or 10.71 per cent till November 23.

Following the bullish trend in equities, the market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies has surged by Rs 34.61 lakh crore to Rs 5,08,98,444.87 crore (USD 5.48 trillion) this month.

Foreign investors have emerged as a major driver behind markets rally, with net investments crossing the Rs 1 lakh crore mark to reach Rs 1.27 lakh crore in November so far, marking the highest-ever monthly inflow.

The strong inflows come after Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) withdrew Rs 34,843 crore in October and Rs 35,861 crore in September, according to data available with the NSDL.

Last week, the BSE benchmark jumped 2,327.26 points, or 2.85 per cent, and the Nifty climbed 656.3 points, or 2.61 per cent.

Markets faced sharp profit-booking on Monday, declining nearly 2 per cent, following a four-week rally.

stories.title: Is stock market open today? Thanksgiving, Black Friday holiday, US trading schedule - Nasdaq, New York Stock Exchange
stories.summary: US stock markets will close for Thanksgiving on November 26 and reopen with an early 1 p.m. ET close on Black Friday. The article also outlines holiday trading hours for bonds and year-end market closures, while reporting a sharp Monday rally led by Nvidia.
stories.text:
**Stock Market holiday:** US stock markets are open for regular trading on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, but investors will soon face a break in the trading calendar as the US prepares to celebrate Thanksgiving. The New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) and Nasdaq will follow their standard trading schedules on Tuesday and Wednesday, before shutting completely on Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving Day. Trading will resume on Friday, November 27, but with an early closing bell for Black Friday. Both exchanges will operate during their regular core trading hours of 9:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) on Tuesday and Wednesday. However, investors should account for the shortened trading week when planning their transactions, particularly as liquidity and trading activity may change around the holiday. The NYSE and Nasdaq will remain closed on Thursday, November 26, in observance of Thanksgiving Day. No regular equity trading sessions will take place, giving investors a full-day break from the markets. Trading will resume on Friday, November 27, although both exchanges will operate on a shortened schedule. The opening bell will ring at the usual 9:30 a.m. ET, but the regular trading session will end at 1:00 p.m. ET, three hours earlier than usual. Options traders will have a slightly longer window, with eligible options contracts scheduled to trade until 1:15 p.m. ET. Certain affiliated electronic trading platforms, including NYSE Arca and Nasdaq extended-hours networks, may offer limited trading opportunities until 5:00 p.m. ET. However, investors should be mindful that liquidity typically thins out after the 1:00 p.m. ET equity market close. Limit orders may therefore offer greater control over execution prices than market orders during these periods. After the Thanksgiving break, Wall Street will return to its regular weekday trading schedule, apart from the remaining holiday adjustments towards the end of 2026. **Thanksgiving Day**: Thursday, November 26 – Full-day market closure. **Day after Thanksgiving (Black Friday): **Friday, November 27 – Early close at 1:00 p.m. ET. **Christmas Eve**: Thursday, December 24 – Early close at 1:00 p.m. ET. **Christmas Day**: Friday, December 25 – Full-day market closure. The US bond market follows a separate holiday timetable recommended by the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (SIFMA). Like equities, the bond market will remain closed on Thursday, November 26, for Thanksgiving. On Friday, November 27, however, fixed-income trading will run from 8:00 a.m. ET until an early close at 2:00 p.m. ET. This gives bond market participants an additional hour of trading compared with equity investors, whose regular session ends at 1:00 p.m. ET. Bond markets will also close early at 2:00 p.m. ET on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve, Thursday, December 31. All US financial markets will remain closed on Friday, January 1, 2027, for New Year's Day. Cryptocurrency markets, meanwhile, operate continuously, 24 hours a day, including throughout the Thanksgiving and Black Friday holiday period. **Wall Street rally: Nvidia surge lifts Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq** US equities staged a powerful recovery on Monday, November 23, with technology stocks leading the rebound after Nvidia's decision to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO revived investor interest in artificial intelligence-related shares. Nvidia, a major driver of the AI trade, surged 31.5%, marking its biggest single-day percentage gain since May 9, 2003. The company had announced Huang's resignation on November 12 following revelations about extramarital affairs, including an alleged relationship with a Chinese spy. US President Donald Trump said he had secured an agreement with Nvidia's board to bring Huang back as CEO. However, the decision also attracted criticism from lawmakers across both political parties, who argued that Congress should tighten restrictions on China's access to Nvidia's advanced AI chips. The rally helped Wall Street recover from the previous week's sharp sell-off, when concerns surrounding the AI trade pushed the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average into correction territory on Friday. The Nasdaq-100 added more than $2 trillion in market value on Monday. The Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 also recorded their biggest single-day percentage gains since the market's rally following Trump's pause of the 'Liberation Day' tariff package in April 2025. At the close, the Dow Jones Industrial Average had jumped 1,447.98 points, or 3.01%, to 49,595.31. The S&P 500 advanced 326.78 points, or 4.73%, to 7,237.17, while the Nasdaq Composite surged 1,471.83 points, or 6.51%, to settle at 24,089.56. *Disclaimer: This story is for educational purposes only.
